Think about how many cards you own. Now multiply each one by 16 digits, an expiry date and a CVV.


For years, that’s what paying online has asked of us. We’ve memorised card numbers, saved photos of our cards in our gallery, emailed card details to ourselves and scribbled them on sticky notes, all so we could type them into the next checkout form. Somewhere along the way, we decided this was normal.


It doesn’t have to be. Payments are moving into a new era, and card payments are finally getting the upgrade they’ve needed.


**Today, we’re launching Samsung Pay on Card Link by Cashfree.**


###


**No more empty card forms**


With Samsung Pay on Card Link, your customers on Samsung Galaxy phones no longer land on a blank card form, even when they’re visiting your site for the first time.


Here’s what paying looks like now:


1. **Tap Samsung Pay** on your checkout.
2. **Select a card** already saved in Samsung Wallet.
3. **Authenticate** with fingerprint, face or PIN.
4. **Payment successful.**


No hunting for card details, no typing and no second attempts after a typo.


###


**From tap-to-pay in stores to checkouts online**


Samsung Pay has been part of how India pays for years. It was one of the early names in tap-to-pay at stores, and Galaxy users already trust it to keep their cards safe and pay with a tap.


With this launch, that same seamlessness comes to online checkouts on Cashfree. The cards your customers have already saved in Samsung Wallet are now ready to use at your checkout too.


###


**Why device tokens change the game**


In India, a card you save on a website is tied to that one merchant. So the first time a customer shops somewhere new, they’re back to typing all 16 digits.


Samsung Pay works differently. When a customer adds a card to Samsung Wallet, the card network replaces the card number with a **device token** , tied to that card and that phone. The token lives on the phone and works across merchants. At checkout, the phone generates a one-time code that’s valid only for that transaction. Only the card network can map the token back to the real card, so the actual card number is never shared with you or Cashfree.


That’s what makes faster, safer first-time payments possible.


###


**What Samsung Pay means for your business**


**3x faster payments** **** Customers go straight to the cards already saved in their Samsung Wallet.


**Higher success rates** **** No manual entry errors, and device-token payments get approved more often.


**Fewer drop-offs** **** Less typing means more customers complete their payment.


**Secure by design** **** Device tokens mean the real card number is never shared with you or Cashfree.


###


**Getting started**


**If you’re on Cashfree hosted web checkout** **** You’re all set. Samsung Pay is already enabled on your checkout (web and mobile web) and shows up automatically for eligible customers. There’s nothing to build or configure.


**If you’re on our Android or hybrid SDK** **** Samsung Pay is available on the SDK too. \[Check the docs\] to see how to enable it.


**Ready to offer Samsung Pay to your customers?** **** Tap the button below, and our team will take it from there.


**<Sign Up>**
